text:
Adam Fox has 26 points in 23 games, 24 of them assists, and he's playing almost 23 minutes a night, up past 24 lately. That's a Norris winner (2020-21) doing exactly what made him one, and Forever Blueshirts already has him in its trophy-case conversation.

The interesting part is that the points are lagging his play. The Rangers have scored 5.8 fewer goals than their chances deserve with him on the ice, and at five on five they've taken about 60% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) in his minutes, 11 points better than when he sits. That gap tends to close in the direction of more points, not fewer.

Evolving-Hockey had him ninth among 215 defensemen in wins above replacement last season, with his impact on both ends of the ice near the top of the league. He's no burner and his shot is ordinary by NHL Edge's tracking; it's all reads and passes.

What to watch: with Igor Shesterkin gone for the season, the Rangers need to outscore problems more often. Fox is how they do it.
